description: Gallantry Awards are presented by the Government of India to military personnel and civilians to honor their exceptional courage, bravery, and sacrifice. These awards are categorized into Wartime and Peacetime gallantry awards.

sections.title: Wartime Gallantry Awards
sections.description: National decorations awarded for conspicuous bravery and indomitable courage in the face of the enemy.

key_concepts.explanation: India's highest military decoration, awarded for unparalleled courage, most conspicuous bravery, or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy.
The second-highest military decoration in India, awarded for acts of outstanding gallantry in the presence of the enemy on the battlefield.
The third-highest wartime military award presented for acts of gallantry and bravery in the battlefield.

sections.title: Peacetime Gallantry Awards
sections.description: Honors awarded for bravery, courage, or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield, during peacetime.

key_concepts.explanation: The highest peacetime gallantry award, awarded for the most conspicuous bravery or some daring or pre-eminent act of valour. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Param Vir Chakra.
The second-highest peacetime gallantry award, given for exceptional bravery away from the battlefield. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Maha Vir Chakra.
The third-highest peacetime gallantry award, awarded for gallantry otherwise than in the face of the enemy. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Vir Chakra.

sections.title: Institution and History
sections.description: Important historical dates related to the institution and naming of India's Gallantry Awards.

historical_events.significance: The Param Vir Chakra (PVC), Maha Vir Chakra (MVC), and Vir Chakra (VrC) were instituted by the President of India, with retrospective effect from 15 August 1947.
The Ashok Chakra Class-I, Class-II, and Class-III were instituted by the Government of India (effective from 15 August 1947).
The three classes of the Ashok Chakra were renamed as Ashok Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra, respectively.

key_associations.item: Flying Officer Nirmal Jit Singh Sekhon

sections.title: Medal Design and Important Facts
sections.description: Information about the structure of the medals and other exam-oriented important facts.

important_facts.fact: The medal of the Param Vir Chakra was designed by Savitri Khanolkar, a Swiss-born woman who was married to an Indian Army officer.
The circular bronze medal of the Param Vir Chakra features four replicas of 'Indra's Vajra' (the mythical weapon made from the bones of Maharishi Dadhichi) surrounding the state emblem in the center.
The Order of Precedence for gallantry awards is: Param Vir Chakra (PVC), Ashok Chakra (AC), Maha Vir Chakra (MVC), Kirti Chakra (KC), Vir Chakra (VrC), and Shaurya Chakra (SC).
Gallantry Awards are announced twice a year by the President of India: on Republic Day and Independence Day.
To date, only 21 military personnel have been awarded the Param Vir Chakra, out of which 14 were awarded posthumously.
